title: Fibre products commute with limits along affine transition morphisms
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and let $(X_i\xrightarrow{f_i}S_i\xleftarrow{g_i}T_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of diagrams of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$: inverse systems $(X_i)$, $(S_i)$, $(T_i)$ whose transition morphisms $X_{i'}\to X_i$, $S_{i'}\to S_i$, $T_{i'}\to T_i$ ($i'\ge i$) are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and commute with the $f_i,g_i$. Let $X=\varprojlim X_i$, $S=\varprojlim S_i$, $T=\varprojlim T_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] and $f:X\to S$, $g:T\to S$ the limit morphisms. Then the induced morphisms $X_{i'}\times_{S_{i'}}T_{i'}\to X_i\times_{S_i}T_i$ of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] are affine, so they form an inverse system with affine transition morphisms, and $X\times_ST$, with the induced morphisms $X\times_ST\to X_i\times_{S_i}T_i$, is its limit in the category of schemes: $X\times_ST=\varprojlim_i(X_i\times_{S_i}T_i)$. In particular, for $s\in S$ with images $s_i\in S_i$, the scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] $X_{s_i}=X_i\times_{S_i}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)$ form an inverse system with affine transition morphisms whose limit is $X_s$ (using $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)=\varprojlim\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)$ over the $S_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-residue-field]).

proof.text: (Limit comparison.) Apply the universal-property lemma [lem-kun-fibre-product-limits] to the compatible inverse systems $(X_i)$, $(S_i)$ and $(T_i)$. The canonical map from the limit of the fibre products to the fibre product of the three limits is an isomorphism. Inverting it and using the given identifications of $X$, $S$, and $T$ with their limits gives $X\times_ST\cong\varprojlim_i(X_i\times_{S_i}T_i)$, with the stated projections.

proof.text: (Affine transition morphisms.) For $i'\ge i$, the three comparison maps $X_{i'}\to X_i$, $S_{i'}\to S_i$, and $T_{i'}\to T_i$ are affine by hypothesis and commute with the structure maps. The induced map $X_{i'}\times_{S_{i'}}T_{i'}\to X_i\times_{S_i}T_i$ is therefore affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-transition]. In detail, the map first factors through the pullback along the affine diagonal of $S_{i'}\to S_i$, and then through the fibre product of the affine maps on $X$ and $T$; stability under base change and composition are Tags 01SD and 01SC, while the affine diagonal/permanence is Tag 01SG. Thus the fibre products form an inverse system with affine transitions.

source.place: Lemmas Tags 01SD, 01SC, and 01SG, applied to the transition square

proof.text: (Scheme-theoretic fibres.) For $s\in S$ with images $s_i\in S_i$, the residue-field limit [lem-weil-pbc-limit-residue-field] identifies $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ with $\varprojlim_i\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)$ over the $S_i$. Apply the same limit-comparison argument of the first step to the diagrams $X_i\to S_i\leftarrow\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)$. It gives $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\cong\varprojlim_i(X_i\times_{S_i}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i))=\varprojlim_iX_{s_i}$. The transition maps of these fibres are affine by the affine-transition lemma in the second step (with $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)$), so they form the asserted affine inverse system.
